sources.structural_source: astro-templates/owl/ (read directly from the repo — the owl template IS the structural source of truth; per the reference-library fragility note, the template directory supersedes scraping owlroofing.com, so no Firecrawl spend was incurred here)
sources.brand_token_source: sites/comprehensive-pain-specialists/intake-scraped.json (Firecrawl branding extraction from the client homepage)
sources.note: No medical/pain-management vertical exists in reference-libraries/. The roofing and concrete libraries are structurally relevant (owl/firefly) but their earth-tone and cyan palettes are wrong for a clinic, so the palette is derived entirely from the client's own brand blues.

contrast_check.accent_ink_on_bg: 10.86:1 (AAA) — accent used as TEXT on light backgrounds
contrast_check.accent_on_primary: 3.55:1 — accent as a non-text mark on the dark navy band, matching the template's light-bg-uses-ink / dark-panel-uses-accent rule
contrast_check.derivation: Client's brand blue #1025A1 is too dark to read on the dark navy panels the owl template uses for Testimonials / ProcessSteps / WhyChooseUs (1.56:1). It is therefore kept as accent-ink for text on light backgrounds, and a lighter sibling #2E5BFF carries the fill/CTA role.

typography.note: Poppins is the client's actual brand font (detected on the live site) and is kept for headings. Body copy moves to Inter — the client's current site sets body text at 12px in Poppins, which is a readability defect for an older patient demographic. Inter at 16px+ fixes it without abandoning the brand voice.

section_styling_hints: Dark navy full-bleed bands (#0A1330) for Testimonials, ProcessSteps, and WhyChooseUs — echoes the client's existing navy identity without copying their layout
Insurance carrier logos rendered as a light, uncluttered PartnerBadges band — the single highest-value trust asset the client already owns
Real clinical/patient photography only, sourced from the client's own site
Generous line-height and 16px+ body copy throughout for an older patient demographic
avoid: generic medical stock photography (smiling doctor with clipboard, stethoscope on desk, handshake)
Lucide icon rows (max 1 outline icon per section, semantic only)
90-item mega-menu navigation — the client's current nav is the #1 usability defect found in the audit
duplicated desktop/mobile content blocks in the same DOM (client's current site does this on every section)
stacking dark navy panels back-to-back with no light section between them
surfacing the 3.2 Google aggregate rating anywhere on the site
'You cannot copy content of this website, your IP is being recorded' style visitor-hostile notices
claiming outcomes, cure rates, or 'best in the area' — this is a medical practice and every claim must trace to something the client actually published
collecting any PHI in a web form beyond name, phone, email, and reason for visit
